testKinds.name: Laboratory test
testKinds.summary: A measurement or observation made on a specimen (blood, urine, another body fluid, a swab or tissue).

testKinds.name: Test panel
testKinds.summary: A named group of laboratory tests reported together; each component is its own test or biomarker.

testKinds.name: Physiological measurement
testKinds.summary: A bedside measurement of the body: blood pressure, pulse, oxygen saturation, temperature, weight.

testKinds.name: Physiological or functional test
testKinds.summary: A recording or functional study without a specimen: ECG, spirometry, EEG, nerve conduction, audiometry.

testKinds.name: Imaging study
testKinds.summary: A picture of the inside of the body made with X-rays, sound, magnetism or a radioactive tracer.

testKinds.name: Diagnostic procedure
testKinds.summary: A procedure done to look inside the body or obtain a sample: endoscopy, catheterisation, lumbar puncture.

testKinds.name: Clinical examination
testKinds.summary: A structured bedside or clinic examination: slit-lamp, fundoscopy, dermoscopy, the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre.

testKinds.name: Screening or assessment tool
testKinds.summary: A validated questionnaire or score used to screen for or grade a condition; proprietary instruments are described, never reproduced.

testKinds.name: Pathology or cytology test
testKinds.summary: Examination of tissue or cells under the microscope, with or without special stains.

testKinds.name: Genetic or molecular test
testKinds.summary: A test of DNA, RNA, chromosomes or gene expression; must state whether it concerns a gene, a variant, a panel or the field in general.

testKinds.name: Microbiology test
testKinds.summary: Detection or culture of bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites, and susceptibility testing.

specimens.name: Venous blood
specimens.summary: Blood drawn from a vein into a tube; the anticoagulant in the tube decides what can be measured.

specimens.name: Whole blood (EDTA)
specimens.summary: Unseparated blood kept from clotting, used for cell counts and HbA1c.

specimens.name: Serum
specimens.summary: The fluid left after blood has clotted; most chemistry and antibody tests.

specimens.name: Plasma
specimens.summary: The fluid part of anticoagulated blood; coagulation tests need citrate plasma.

specimens.name: Serum or plasma
specimens.summary: Either serum or plasma is acceptable for the measurement.

specimens.name: Capillary (fingerprick) blood
specimens.summary: A drop of blood from a fingerprick or heel prick, used by point-of-care devices.

specimens.name: Arterial blood
specimens.summary: Blood taken from an artery for blood-gas analysis.

specimens.name: Urine (spot sample)
specimens.summary: A single urine sample, ideally the first of the morning for some tests.

specimens.name: Midstream urine
specimens.summary: A clean-catch sample from the middle of the stream, for culture and dipstick.

specimens.name: 24-hour urine collection
specimens.summary: All urine passed over 24 hours, for excretion rates.

specimens.name: Stool
specimens.summary: A faeces sample for occult blood, calprotectin, culture, parasites or antigens.

specimens.name: Cerebrospinal fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid obtained by lumbar puncture.

specimens.name: Sputum
specimens.summary: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.

specimens.name: Throat swab
specimens.summary: A swab of the tonsils and pharynx.

specimens.name: Nose or nasopharyngeal swab
specimens.summary: A swab of the nose or nasopharynx, for respiratory viruses and bacteria.

specimens.name: Wound or skin swab
specimens.summary: A swab of a wound, ulcer or skin lesion.

specimens.name: Genital swab
specimens.summary: A vaginal, cervical, urethral or rectal swab, often self-taken.

specimens.name: Tissue
specimens.summary: A biopsy or surgical specimen for histopathology.

specimens.name: Cytology sample
specimens.summary: Cells scraped, brushed or aspirated from a surface or a lump.

specimens.name: Bone marrow
specimens.summary: Aspirate or trephine biopsy of the marrow, usually from the hip bone.

specimens.name: Pleural fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid drawn from around the lung.

specimens.name: Peritoneal (ascitic) fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid drawn from the abdominal cavity.

specimens.name: Synovial (joint) fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid aspirated from a joint.

specimens.name: Pericardial fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid drawn from around the heart.

specimens.name: Amniotic fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid drawn from around the fetus.

specimens.name: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
specimens.summary: Fluid washed out of the airways during bronchoscopy.

specimens.name: Semen
specimens.summary: A semen sample for fertility or post-vasectomy testing.

specimens.name: Saliva
specimens.summary: Saliva collected for hormone or DNA testing.

specimens.name: Exhaled breath
specimens.summary: Breath samples for hydrogen, urea or nitric-oxide tests.

specimens.name: Hair or nail
specimens.summary: Hair or nail clippings for toxicology or fungal culture.

specimens.name: No specimen
specimens.summary: A recording, image, measurement or examination rather than a sample.

methods.name: Automated cell counter
methods.summary: Cells counted and sized by an analyser as they pass a detector.

methods.name: Microscopy
methods.summary: Direct examination of a sample under the microscope, with or without staining.

methods.name: Blood film examination
methods.summary: A stained smear of blood examined for cell shape and abnormal cells.

methods.name: Flow cytometry
methods.summary: Cells labelled with fluorescent antibodies and counted by type.

methods.name: Clot-based coagulation assay
methods.summary: The time to form a clot after a reagent is added to citrated plasma.

methods.name: Chemistry analyser
methods.summary: Automated spectrophotometric or electrode-based measurement of a substance.

methods.name: Immunoassay
methods.summary: Detection of a substance by its binding to a specific antibody.

methods.name: Electrophoresis
methods.summary: Separation of proteins or haemoglobins by their movement in an electric field.

methods.name: Chromatography and mass spectrometry
methods.summary: Separation and identification of molecules by mass; the reference method for many hormones and drugs.

methods.name: Culture
methods.summary: Growing organisms from a sample on nutrient media.

methods.name: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing
methods.summary: Testing which antimicrobials inhibit a cultured organism.

methods.name: Antigen detection
methods.summary: Detection of a component of an organism, often as a rapid test.

methods.name: Serology (antibody detection)
methods.summary: Detection of the antibodies the immune system has made against an organism or the body's own tissues.

methods.name: PCR (including RT-PCR and qPCR)
methods.summary: Amplification of a specific DNA or RNA sequence to detect or quantify it.

methods.name: Nucleic acid amplification test
methods.summary: Any technique that amplifies an organism's genetic material, PCR included.

methods.name: DNA sequencing
methods.summary: Reading the order of bases in a gene, a panel of genes, the exome or the whole genome.

methods.name: Karyotype
methods.summary: Chromosomes photographed and arranged from dividing cells.

methods.name: Fluorescence in situ hybridisation
methods.summary: Fluorescent probes that light up specific chromosome regions.

methods.name: Chromosomal microarray
methods.summary: Detection of gained or lost chromosome segments across the genome.

methods.name: Methylation analysis
methods.summary: Testing the chemical marks that switch genes on or off.

methods.name: Immunohistochemistry
methods.summary: Antibody stains applied to tissue sections to identify proteins.

methods.name: Immunofluorescence
methods.summary: Fluorescent antibody stains on tissue or cells.

methods.name: Histology
methods.summary: Fixed, sectioned and stained tissue examined under the microscope.

methods.name: Cytology
methods.summary: Individual cells examined under the microscope.

methods.name: Electron microscopy
methods.summary: Very high magnification imaging of tissue ultrastructure.

methods.name: Dipstick
methods.summary: A reagent strip that changes colour when dipped into a sample.

methods.name: Point-of-care device
methods.summary: A meter or cartridge test run at the bedside or at home.

methods.name: Electrophysiological recording
methods.summary: Recording the electrical activity of the heart, brain, nerves or muscles.

methods.name: Ultrasound
methods.summary: Images from high-frequency sound reflected by tissues.

methods.name: Radiography
methods.summary: Images made with X-rays.

methods.name: Computed tomography
methods.summary: Cross-sectional X-ray images reconstructed by computer.

methods.name: Magnetic resonance imaging
methods.summary: Images made with a strong magnetic field and radio waves.

methods.name: Nuclear medicine
methods.summary: Images of where a radioactive tracer accumulates.

methods.name: Spirometry
methods.summary: Measurement of the volume and speed of a forced breath out.

methods.name: Body plethysmography
methods.summary: Lung volumes measured in a sealed cabin.

methods.name: Gas transfer (DLCO)
methods.summary: How well a test gas crosses from the lungs into blood.

methods.name: Pulse oximetry
methods.summary: Oxygen saturation estimated from light passed through a fingertip.

methods.name: Endoscopy
methods.summary: A camera passed into the body through a natural opening or a small cut.

methods.name: Biopsy
methods.summary: Removal of a sample of tissue for examination.

methods.name: Manometry
methods.summary: Pressure measurements inside a hollow organ.

methods.name: pH monitoring
methods.summary: Acidity recorded over time by a probe.

methods.name: Breath test
methods.summary: Analysis of gases in exhaled breath after a test substance.

methods.name: Audiometry
methods.summary: Hearing thresholds measured with tones or speech.

methods.name: Tonometry
methods.summary: Measurement of the pressure inside the eye.

methods.name: Questionnaire or score
methods.summary: A validated set of questions or a scoring system.

methods.name: Clinical examination
methods.summary: A structured examination by a clinician.

methods.name: Physical measurement
methods.summary: A measurement with a cuff, thermometer, scale or tape.

methods.name: Calculation from other results
methods.summary: A value derived from other measurements by a formula.

imagingModalities.name: X-ray (radiography)
imagingModalities.summary: Plain X-ray images, including mammography and dental films.

imagingModalities.name: Fluoroscopy
imagingModalities.summary: Real-time X-ray imaging, used for contrast studies and guided procedures.

imagingModalities.name: Mammography
imagingModalities.summary: Low-dose X-ray imaging of the breast.

imagingModalities.name: Ultrasound
imagingModalities.summary: Sound-wave imaging, including Doppler studies of blood flow and echocardiography.

imagingModalities.name: CT (computed tomography)
imagingModalities.summary: Cross-sectional X-ray imaging, with or without contrast.

imagingModalities.name: MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
imagingModalities.summary: Magnetic-field imaging, including angiography, spectroscopy and functional MRI.

imagingModalities.name: PET (positron emission tomography)
imagingModalities.summary: Imaging of a positron-emitting tracer, usually combined with CT or MRI.

imagingModalities.name: DXA bone densitometry
imagingModalities.summary: Two X-ray energies used to measure bone mineral density.

imagingModalities.name: Catheter angiography
imagingModalities.summary: Contrast injected through a catheter under fluoroscopy to image vessels.

routes.name: Buccal
routes.summary: Held against the inside of the cheek.

routes.name: Topical
routes.summary: Applied to the skin or a surface.

routes.name: Transdermal
routes.summary: Absorbed through the skin from a patch or gel into the bloodstream.

routes.name: Nebulised
routes.summary: Breathed in as a mist from a nebuliser.

routes.name: Intravenous
routes.summary: Injected or infused into a vein.

routes.name: Intraosseous
routes.summary: Into the bone marrow, an emergency alternative to a vein.

routes.name: Intrathecal
routes.summary: Into the fluid around the spinal cord.

routes.name: Epidural
routes.summary: Into the space outside the membranes of the spinal cord.

routes.name: Intravitreal
routes.summary: Into the jelly of the eye.

routes.name: Intracameral
routes.summary: Into the front chamber of the eye.

routes.name: Implant
routes.summary: Placed under the skin or in a tissue to release the medicine over months.

routes.name: Local infiltration
routes.summary: Injected into the tissue to be numbed or treated.

routes.name: Enteral tube
routes.summary: Given through a feeding tube into the stomach or intestine.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Prescription only
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Supplied only against a prescription (UK POM, US Rx-only).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Over the counter
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Sold without a prescription in general retail (UK GSL).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Pharmacy or behind the counter
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Sold without a prescription but only from a pharmacy, under a pharmacist's supervision (UK P).

regulatoryStatuses.name: Controlled substance
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Additional legal controls on prescribing, supply and possession (UK Misuse of Drugs schedules, US DEA schedules); always in addition to prescription status.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Specialist or restricted
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Prescribed only by, or on the advice of, a specialist, or within a restricted-access programme.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Hospital only
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Supplied and administered only in hospital.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Emergency-use authorisation
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Authorised under an emergency or conditional mechanism rather than a full licence.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Discontinued
regulatoryStatuses.summary: No longer marketed in the jurisdiction, though the licence may remain.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Withdrawn
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Licence withdrawn or suspended, usually for safety reasons.

regulatoryStatuses.name: Investigational
regulatoryStatuses.summary: Not licensed; available only in clinical trials or on a named-patient basis.

productTypes.name: Small-molecule medicine
productTypes.summary: A chemically synthesised medicine, the majority of tablets, capsules and injections.

productTypes.name: Biologic
productTypes.summary: A medicine made by or from living cells: antibodies, recombinant proteins, enzymes, cytokines, clotting factors, immunoglobulins. A product type, not a therapeutic class.

productTypes.name: Biosimilar
productTypes.summary: A biologic shown to be highly similar to an already licensed reference biologic.

productTypes.name: Monoclonal antibody
productTypes.summary: An antibody engineered to bind one target (names ending in -mab).

productTypes.name: Recombinant protein or hormone
productTypes.summary: A human protein made by engineered cells: insulins, growth hormone, erythropoietins, enzymes, clotting factors.

productTypes.name: Vaccine
productTypes.summary: A product that trains the immune system against a disease target.

productTypes.name: Blood-derived product
productTypes.summary: Immunoglobulins, albumin, clotting-factor concentrates and other products prepared from blood or plasma.

productTypes.name: Gene therapy
productTypes.summary: A product that adds, replaces or edits genetic material in a person's cells.

productTypes.name: Cell therapy
productTypes.summary: Living cells given as treatment: CAR-T cells, other engineered immune cells, stem-cell-derived products.

productTypes.name: Radiopharmaceutical
productTypes.summary: A radioactive medicine used for imaging (diagnostic) or treatment (therapeutic).

productTypes.name: Contrast agent
productTypes.summary: A substance given to make blood vessels, organs or cavities show up on imaging.

productTypes.name: Diagnostic agent
productTypes.summary: A dye, tracer or challenge substance used in a test rather than as treatment.

productTypes.name: Intravenous fluid
productTypes.summary: Crystalloid or colloid solutions given into a vein.

productTypes.name: Electrolyte preparation
productTypes.summary: Potassium, magnesium, calcium, phosphate or bicarbonate preparations.

productTypes.name: Herbal medicine or supplement
productTypes.summary: A product regulated as a herbal medicine or supplement rather than a licensed medicine.

productTypes.name: Other product type
productTypes.summary: A product that fits none of the other types.

atcGroups.name: Systemic hormonal preparations, excluding sex hormones and insulins

molecularScopes.name: A panel of genes or variants
A field of testing described in general

testRelationships.summary: The analyte or component a test reports (from components[].biomarker and biomarkers[]).
The organ or atlas structure the test looks at (anatomy.organs, anatomy.structures).
The body system the test looks at (anatomy.systems).
A condition the test may help evaluate (conditions[]); never 'proves'.
A condition the test is used to monitor over time (monitors[]).
A medicine whose sourced monitoring plan names the test (computed from medications[].monitoringPlan).
A symptom that commonly leads to the test (symptoms[]).
A panel and the individual test it contains (components[].test).
Preparation the person must make (preparation), when there is any.
An authoritative source cited on the page (references[]).

medicationRelationships.summary: A brand or combination product and each active ingredient it contains (products.json).
A brand name, with the jurisdiction it is sold in (brands{}).
A licensed or guideline-supported indication with its source (indications[]).
A side effect listed in the cited source (sideEffects).
A sourced interaction record (interactions.json); the target may be a class or a named medicine.
A test or biomarker in the sourced monitoring plan (monitoringPlan[]).
An organ or structure the medicine acts on (anatomy.organs, anatomy.structures).
A body system the medicine acts on (anatomy.systems).
A physiological process the medicine changes (physiology[]).
The organ that metabolises the medicine, from the sourced pharmacokinetics (pharmacokinetics.metabolism).
The organ that eliminates the medicine, from the sourced pharmacokinetics (pharmacokinetics.elimination).
A related medicine that is not a synonym and not necessarily the same class (related[]).

reviewQueues.summary: Entities with fewer than two references, or a structured fact whose source is missing (the build already fails on the latter).
Entities whose review status is before clinical review.
Two pages, or a catalogued concept and a page, with the same normalised name.
An alias that is also the name or alias of another entity of the same kind (a same-class medicine or a sub-test presented as 'also known as').
A brand name listed under more than one ingredient, or an alias that looks like a brand but is not in the brands table.
A product ingredient given as free text although a medication page with that name exists.
A medicine whose drugClass differs from the class that lists it as a member, or an alias that names a class.
Interaction records left at needs-review because their sources disagree.
A test whose text quotes numeric cut-offs without a sourced, jurisdiction-tagged threshold record.
Two regulatory entries for the same jurisdiction with different statuses and no note explaining why.
Terminology mappings flagged deprecated or discouraged by the terminology release.
Indexable pages with little body text or a single reference.
Catalogued test concepts and taxonomy classes that have no public page yet, by category (not thin pages: they are database-only until written).

provenanceFields.summary: The terminology or document the record was taken from.
Release or version of that source.
When a person or the pipeline last verified the record against its source.
When a clinician reviewed the record.
